categories_allocable_help: Costs linked to the use of the property are allocable (Art. 257a–257b Code of Obligations, CO), e.g. heating, water, caretaker. Repairs, renewals, building insurance and taxes are borne by the landlord; for the heating and the lift only operation and servicing of the system count. For water, waste water and waste, base fees that depend on the value of the property do not count; for waste water the rainwater fee does not count either. The tenant pays allocable costs only if the rental contract names each of these cost types separately (Art. 257a para. 2 CO).
categories_reason_heating: Fuel, energy, servicing and operation of the heating are chargeable (Art. 5 Tenancy Ordinance, VMWG); repair, renewal, interest and depreciation of the system are not (Art. 6 VMWG). The running heating costs are therefore allocable.
categories_reason_hot_water: Energy and operation of the central hot water supply are chargeable (Art. 5 para. 1 Tenancy Ordinance, VMWG); repair and renewal of the system are not (Art. 6 VMWG). The running hot water costs are therefore allocable.
categories_reason_cold_water: The water used is linked to the use (Art. 257b para. 1 Code of Obligations, CO); base fees that depend on the value of the property are not. The water used is therefore allocable.
categories_reason_wastewater: The fee by consumption is linked to the use (Art. 257b para. 1 Code of Obligations, CO); the rainwater fee and base fees that depend on the value of the property are not. The fee by consumption is therefore allocable.
categories_reason_common_electricity: Electricity for shared rooms and outdoor lighting is linked to the use (Art. 257a para. 1 Code of Obligations, CO), and therefore allocable.
categories_reason_elevator: Electricity, emergency phone and servicing of the lift are linked to the use (Art. 257a para. 1 Code of Obligations, CO); repairs and spare parts are borne by the landlord. If a full-service contract also covers repairs, only its servicing share is allocable: add only that share under «Lift». Electricity, emergency phone and servicing are therefore allocable.
categories_reason_caretaker: Cleaning, running the heating and minor upkeep are linked to the use (Art. 257a para. 1 Code of Obligations, CO); administration and repairs are not. Caretaking is therefore allocable.
categories_reason_garden: Ongoing care of the grounds is linked to the use (Art. 257a para. 1 Code of Obligations, CO); new planting and purchases are not. Ongoing care is therefore allocable.
categories_reason_snow: Snow clearing and gritting are linked to the use (Art. 257a para. 1 Code of Obligations, CO); buying equipment is not. Snow clearing and gritting are therefore allocable.
categories_reason_waste: Waste fees based on use (e.g. a base fee per apartment, a container by weight) are public charges arising from the use of the property (Art. 257b para. 1 Code of Obligations, CO); base fees that depend on the value of the property and clearances the landlord orders are not. These waste fees are therefore allocable.
categories_reason_tv: The ongoing base fee of the cable network is linked to the use (Art. 257a para. 1 Code of Obligations, CO); installing the connection is not. The base fee is therefore allocable.
categories_reason_chimney: Cleaning the chimney and the heating system is part of the heating costs (Art. 5 para. 2 let. d Tenancy Ordinance, VMWG), and therefore allocable.
categories_reason_repairs: The landlord must keep the property fit for use (Art. 256 para. 1 Code of Obligations, CO). Repairs are covered by the rent, and therefore not allocable.
categories_reason_building_insurance: The premiums are among the burdens of the property that the landlord bears (Art. 256b Code of Obligations, CO); premiums insuring only the heating system belong to the heating (Art. 5 para. 2 let. h Tenancy Ordinance, VMWG). Building insurance is therefore not allocable.
categories_reason_property_tax: Taxes on the property are borne by the landlord (Art. 256b Code of Obligations, CO), and therefore not allocable.
categories_reason_mortgage: Financing the property is not linked to the use (Art. 257a para. 1 Code of Obligations, CO); it is covered by the rent, and therefore not allocable.
categories_reason_administration: General administration is covered by the rent. The work for the utility cost statement can be charged through the management fee (Art. 4 para. 3 Tenancy Ordinance, VMWG) if the rental contract names it (Art. 257a para. 2 Code of Obligations, CO); administrative work for running the heating is part of the heating costs (Art. 5 para. 2 let. i VMWG). General administration is therefore not allocable.
categories_reason_renovation: Renovations keep the building fit for use; that is the landlord’s duty (Art. 256 para. 1 Code of Obligations, CO) and covered by the rent. The part that adds value can justify a rent increase. Renovations are therefore not allocable.
categories_reason_capital_improvements: Investments increase the value of the property and are not linked to the use. They can justify a rent increase (Art. 269a let. b Code of Obligations, CO; Art. 14 Tenancy Ordinance, VMWG). Investments are therefore not allocable.
categories_reason_pest_control: Whether pest control is linked to the use (Art. 257a para. 1 Code of Obligations, CO) is disputed; the Swiss-German tenants’ association Mieterinnen- und Mieterverband counts it among the utility costs that may not be charged (leaflet «Zulässige und unzulässige Nebenkosten»). Dwello follows the leaflet: pest control is therefore not allocable.
categories_reason_fire_extinguisher: Whether servicing fire extinguishers is linked to the use (Art. 257a para. 1 Code of Obligations, CO) is disputed (Swiss-German tenants’ association Mieterinnen- und Mieterverband, leaflet «Zulässige und unzulässige Nebenkosten»). According to the leaflet, fire protection that is needed even when the building stands empty is not a utility cost. Dwello follows the leaflet: the servicing is therefore not allocable.

If a tenant moves in or out during the billing period, Dwello spreads these costs over the months by the heating profile, all others by day. Separately billed hot water is used about evenly all year: leave the box unticked for it.

categories_fuel_help: Tick the box if the invoices of this category are deliveries of heating fuel for a tank or store, for example heating oil, LPG, pellets or wood. For this category you add the fuel stock on the building’s page, so Dwello bills the consumption and not the purchase. Mains natural gas, district heating and electricity have no fuel stock. A category only for servicing or the chimney sweep is not fuel.

contracts_next_steps_text_successor: The rental contract has been terminated and the new tenant is recorded. Ask {name} for the new address and enter it in the tenant’s details. The utility cost statement goes there.
contracts_next_steps_address: Ask {name} for the new address and enter it in the tenant’s details. The utility cost statement goes there.
contracts_next_steps_hint: You can see the next steps at the top of the page.
contracts_apartment_contracts_unknown_te: Dwello could not load the rental contracts for this apartment. Choose «Try again»; your entries are kept. When you save, Dwello always checks whether the period overlaps with another rental contract for this apartment.
contracts_apartment_contracts_loaded: The apartment’s rental contracts are loaded.
contracts_apartment_contracts_retry_fail: The apartment’s rental contracts still could not be loaded. Try again later; your entries are kept.
contracts_apartment_contracts_see_apartm: The rental contracts for this apartment are still missing, see the apartment above.
contracts_delete_draft_contracts_unknown: Dwello did not delete the draft: without the rental contracts for this apartment an overlap cannot be ruled out. Choose «Try again» at the apartment, then «Delete draft and save rental contract» again.
contracts_apartment_contracts_loading: The apartment’s rental contracts are still loading. Try again in a moment.
contracts_notice_hint_text: Then enter the contract end on the rental contract page with «End contract». The contract stays open-ended, and Dwello shows the next steps.
tenants_document_file_help: PDF, JPG or PNG, at most 10 MB. Delete copies of ID documents and debt collection register extracts as soon as you no longer need them.
tenants_document_title_help: Without a title, the document is named after the file, without its extension.
tenants_document_demo: Every visitor sees the files you upload here. Upload only made-up documents.
tenants_document_upload_failed: The document was not saved because Dwello did not respond. Choose «Upload document» again.
tenants_document_delete_text: Document «{title}» will be deleted permanently. This cannot be undone.
tenants_document_delete_failed: The document was not deleted. Try again.
tenants_delete_text_with_documents: {name} will be deleted permanently, together with the uploaded documents. This cannot be undone.
backend_document_too_large: The file is larger than {megabytes} MB. Choose a smaller file or reduce the size of the scan.
backend_document_type_not_allowed: Dwello accepts only PDF, JPG and PNG files. Save the file as a PDF and choose it again.
backend_document_not_deletable: Reminders are kept because they prove that the tenant was reminded.
documents_empty_to_send_text: Letters you have to print and post appear here.
tenants_delete_has_contracts_documents: Tenants with rental contracts are kept because statements and documents refer to them. The documents you uploaded for this tenant stay saved too. Delete them one by one under «Documents» on this page as soon as you no longer need them.
backend_document_title_too_long: The title is longer than {max} characters. Shorten it.
backend_tenant_not_found: This tenant no longer exists. They were probably deleted in another window. Open the list «Tenants».
categories_error_allocable_required: Choose whether the costs are allocable.
backend_ki_proposal_unavailable: The AI cannot be reached. Try again later or decide yourself whether the costs are allocable.
backend_ki_proposal_unsure: The AI is not sure. Decide yourself whether the costs are allocable; the rules are in the help text above. If in doubt: not allocable.
categories_allocable_yes: The costs go into the utility cost statement.
categories_allocable_no: The costs are borne by the landlord.
categories_proposal_checking: The AI is checking the category …
categories_proposal_applied: Dwello has preselected this choice. You decide: check the reasoning and change the choice if it does not fit.
categories_proposal_kept: Your choice stays. Compare it with the AI’s reasoning.
contracts_fixed_term_question: The fixed-term rental contract of {name} expired on {date}. Does {name} still live in the apartment, and do you agree, for example because you keep accepting the rent? Then the rental contract continues open-ended.
contracts_fixed_term_objection: If you do not agree, demand the return of the apartment in writing at once and get advice. If you have accepted the rent for an extended period after the contract end, the rental contract has usually already become open-ended and ends only with a notice of termination.
contracts_continued_toast: The rental contract of {name} continues open-ended. It ends only with a notice of termination.
contracts_draft_deleted_continued_toast: Draft {number} deleted. The rental contract of {name} continues open-ended. Now create the utility cost statement again.
contracts_continue_locked_rest: Dwello does not change them, so Dwello cannot remove the contract end yet. For you and the tenant the rental contract still continues open-ended. First correct each of these statements. Open them and choose «Correct statement».
contracts_fixed_term_consequences: If the rental contract continues, Dwello bills the utility costs after {date} to {name}. If {name} has moved out, the apartment counts as vacant since then, and you bear the utility costs of that time.
contracts_moved_out_consequence: The rental contract ended on {date}. Since then the apartment counts as vacant, and you bear the utility costs of that time. Dwello will no longer ask whether the rental contract continues.
audit_purpose: Sign-ins and changes that affect your statements, with date and time. The entries stay until you delete them.
audit_link: Sign-ins and changes that affect your statements, with their date
audit_empty_text: Sign-ins, changes of the proposed management fee and of whether categories and invoices are allocable, reset payments and corrected statements appear here.
audit_fee: Suggested management fee changed from {from} % to {to} %
audit_category_excluded: Category «{name}»: changed from allocable to not allocable
audit_category_excluded_invoice: Category «{name}»: changed from allocable to not allocable; 1 invoice is therefore no longer allocable
audit_category_excluded_invoices: Category «{name}»: changed from allocable to not allocable; {count} invoices are therefore no longer allocable
audit_category_included: Category «{name}»: changed from not allocable to allocable; invoices of the category that are not allocable stay not allocable
audit_invoice_excluded: Invoice «{description}» from {supplier} dated {date} for {amount} ({building}): marked as not allocable
audit_invoice_included: Invoice «{description}» from {supplier} dated {date} for {amount} ({building}): marked as allocable again
audit_statement_corrected: Statement {number} replaced by a corrected statement
audit_delete_text: The entry of {when} will be deleted from the log for good: {text}. Only the entry is deleted, not what it records. This cannot be undone.
audit_delete_failed: The entry could not be deleted. Please try again.
audit_privacy: So that you can later trace what changed, Dwello records in the log under «Settings», with date and time: each sign-in with the chosen provider or with a password (without name or email address), changes to the management fee and to the allocability of categories, invoices that are no longer or again allocable (with invoice issuer, description, date, amount and building), reset payments (with statement number and payment date), and statements replaced by a corrected statement (with their number), and each change of the AI with its provider and country. The entries stay, even if you delete the invoice, until you delete them in the log. The server log (see «Sign-in») is separate from it.
audit_privacy_demo: In the demo, all visitors see the log with the others’ sign-ins, without name or email address, and can delete entries.
privacy_stored_country: The server is located in the following country: {country}.
privacy_controller_4: Likewise, these people can ask you, and you can ask the operator, to correct inaccurate data (Art. 32(1) FADP) and to hand over the data they provided themselves in a conventional electronic format (Art. 28 FADP). Against unlawful processing they can demand, in court if need be, that it stops or that the data is deleted (Art. 32(2) FADP); what must be retained stays until the end of the retention period. Anyone who suspects a breach of data protection can report it to the Federal Data Protection and Information Commissioner (FDPIC) (Art. 49 FADP).
privacy_mail_smtp_provider: Utility cost statements, payment reminders and further reminders sent by email are delivered through the mail server of {provider} ({country}). {provider} then receives the tenant’s name and email address and the message with the attached PDF: for a reminder, the address and the amount due; for a utility cost statement, the correspondence address, the apartment and the rental period, the costs and how they are shared, the balance, and the IBAN and payment reference.
terms_no_contract: These notes do not replace a contract. If a provider runs Dwello for you, your agreements with that provider apply.
terms_processor: Conclude a data processing agreement with such a provider: it processes the data only in the way you yourself may, keeps it secure and uses other services, for example for sending email or for the AI, only with your prior approval (Art. 9 FADP).
terms_responsibility_3: For this you can pass on to your tenants the sections «Controller», «What data Dwello stores», «Retention» and «Sharing with third parties» of the privacy notice. Tell them your name and how to reach you, and explain that «you» there means the landlord (Art. 19(2) FADP).
terms_responsibility_4: Give this information to your tenants when you receive their data, usually when the rental contract is concluded, on paper or by email. If you do not receive the data from the tenant themselves, for example when you buy a building that is already let, give them this information within one month at the latest (Art. 19(5) FADP). Send it once to your current tenants. You can leave out sentences that concern only you, for example about the sign-in, the log under «Settings» or unsaved entries in the browser.
terms_responsibility_5: If a tenant asks what data you hold about them or for a copy of it, download it on their page with «Export data» and give them the file together with this information (Art. 25 and 28 FADP).
backend_reminder_previous_not_sent: «{reminderLevel}» has not been sent yet. Mark it as sent under «Documents». The next reminder level is possible once its payment deadline has passed.
backend_reminder_statement_paid: The statement has already been paid. Do not send this reminder any more.
backend_reminder_statement_replaced: The statement has been replaced by a corrected statement. Do not send this reminder any more.
statements_reminder_no_email: No email address has been added for {tenant}. Dwello creates the reminder as a PDF. It will then be under «Documents» for printing. «{next}» is in {language}. Mark the letter as sent there on the day you post it.
statements_send_email_bounce: If the email later comes back as undeliverable, deliver the statement by letter. In that case, only send a reminder once the tenant has received the statement by letter and the payment deadline has then passed.
statements_send_no_email: No email address has been added for {tenant}.
documents_not_to_send_paid: Do not send any more: statement paid
documents_not_to_send_replaced: Do not send any more: statement replaced
login_intro_password: Sign in with the email address and password set when Dwello was set up.
login_password_forgot: Forgot your password? The operator of your Dwello installation resets it with a command. If you run Dwello yourself, the command is in the installation guide.
login_error_invalid: The email address or password is not correct. Check what you entered and try again.
login_error_locked: After several failed attempts, sign-in is locked until {time}. Try again then, or have the operator of your Dwello installation lift the lock.
login_insecure_text: Your password and all data, including your tenants’, cross the network unprotected. Have Dwello set up with HTTPS, or use it only through a VPN.
backend_invalid_credentials: The email address or password is not correct. Check what you entered and try again.
backend_account_locked: After several failed attempts, sign-in is locked. Try again later.
backend_password_too_short: The password is too short. Choose one with at least {min} characters, best a long one you use nowhere else.
privacy_login_local_1: You sign in with email address and password; you create the account when you set up Dwello, or the operator creates it for you. For this, Dwello stores your email address and the password only in a transformed form (a hash): the password cannot be calculated back from it, only guessed by trying. So choose a long password that you use nowhere else. Dwello also stores the number of failed attempts and the end of a lock until the next successful sign-in. The header shows your email address.
privacy_login_local_log: Every failed attempt with a password and every lock is recorded in the server log with the email address entered, without the IP address.
setup_intro: Create the password account you sign in to Dwello with. You are then signed in.
setup_code_help: It is in the server log: on the server, enter the command docker logs dwello-backend. The code shown last is the valid one.
setup_password_help: At least 8 characters; best a long password you use nowhere else.
setup_error_repeat: The two passwords do not match. Enter the same password twice.
setup_error_locked: After several wrong setup codes, the setup is locked until {time}. Try again after that.
backend_setup_code_invalid: The setup code is wrong. You find it in the server log with the command docker logs dwello-backend; the code shown last is the valid one. Enter it again.
backend_setup_done: Dwello is already set up. Sign in with your account.
backend_setup_locked: After several wrong setup codes, the setup is locked for 15 minutes. Try again after that.
ki_model_loading_title: The AI model is being downloaded: {percent} %.
ki_model_loading_text: Until it is downloaded, enter invoices by hand.
ki_model_failed_title: The AI model could not be downloaded.
ki_model_failed_text: Enter invoices by hand. Dwello tries again when the operator restarts Dwello; if you run Dwello yourself, the command is in the installation guide.
privacy_third_ollama: If the local AI’s model is missing, Dwello downloads it from Ollama (Ollama Inc., USA), about 6 GB: at start, when you choose the local AI, and when you download it again under «Settings» › «AI». Ollama receives the server’s IP address and the model’s name, no data you enter in Dwello; the details may reach the USA.
setup_error_empty: Fill in every field: the setup code, your email address and the password twice.
backend_email_unusable: Dwello cannot use this email address. Enter an address like name@example.ch.
ki_settings_purpose: Choose the AI that reads and categorises invoices.
ki_settings_link: Local AI, an AI provider or no AI
ki_settings_local_help: Invoices and categories do not leave the server. The local AI needs about 16 GB of memory; Dwello downloads the AI model, about 6 GB.
ki_settings_provider_help: Invoices, invoice files and categories go to the provider, including any names and addresses in them. You need an account there and an API key.
ki_settings_base_url_help: The address the provider gives you for an OpenAI-compatible interface.
ki_settings_api_key_stored: An API key is stored. Leave the field empty to keep it.
ki_settings_model_help: A model that reads images, so that Dwello can read uploaded invoices.
ki_settings_provider_country: Country where the provider processes the data
ki_settings_checklist_1: You have a contract with the provider under which it processes the data only on your behalf, protects it and does not use it to train its AI (Art. 9 FADP). It engages other companies only with your consent. If the AI runs on a server you run yourself, this point does not apply.
ki_settings_checklist_2: The provider and every company it engages process the data only in Switzerland or in a country whose data protection the Federal Council recognises as adequate (Art. 16 para. 1 FADP); in the USA only companies certified under the Swiss-U.S. Data Privacy Framework. Dwello does not support other providers: the privacy statement cannot name additional safeguards.
ki_settings_checklist_3: The provider keeps the data no longer than necessary, ideally not at all or only briefly.
ki_settings_checklist_note: This is a checklist, not legal advice.
ki_settings_confirm: I have checked these three points for this provider.
ki_settings_saved: The AI setting is saved. The next invoice will use it.
ki_settings_not_saved: The AI setting was not saved
ki_settings_missing_confirmed: Confirm that you have checked the three data protection points.
ki_settings_missing_provider: Enter the name of the provider. The privacy statement names it.
ki_settings_missing_country: Enter the country where the provider processes the data. The privacy statement names it.
ki_settings_missing_base_url: Enter the AI address the provider gives you, for example https://api.provider.ch/v1.
ki_settings_missing_model: Enter the model. Choose one that reads images.
ki_settings_check_ok: The connection works, and the model reads invoice images.
ki_settings_check_wrong_key: The provider refuses the API key. Check the key in your account with the provider and enter it again.
ki_settings_check_unreachable: No AI answers at this address. Check the address and whether the server reaches the internet.
ki_settings_check_no_images: The model does not read images. Choose a model that reads images; otherwise Dwello cannot read uploaded invoices.
ki_settings_locked: Set by the operator in the configuration file. If you run Dwello yourself, change the AI there; otherwise contact the operator.
ki_settings_model_failed: Check that the server reaches the internet and has about 6 GB of free space, then download it again. If someone else runs Dwello, contact the operator.
ki_settings_model_offline: The local AI does not answer. Until it does, enter invoices by hand. If you run Dwello yourself, start the local AI as the installation guide describes; otherwise contact the operator or choose a provider or no AI above.
backend_ki_set_by_operator: The AI is set by the operator in the configuration file and cannot be changed here.
backend_ki_not_local: The AI model is downloaded only for the local AI. Choose «Local AI on this server» first.
backend_ki_provider_incomplete: Details of the provider are missing. Fill in the marked fields.
backend_ki_key_for_new_address: Enter the API key again. Dwello does not send the stored key to another address.
backend_ki_encryption_key_missing: The server has no key to store the API key encrypted. The operator sets ENCRYPTION_KEY as the installation guide describes.
ki_settings_provider_name_help: The company’s name as it appears in your contract with it. The privacy statement names it. If the AI runs on a server you run yourself, write your name and «own server». If several companies process the data, name them all, separated by commas.
ki_settings_country_help: The countries where the provider and the companies it engages process the data, even if they only access it. They are usually in the contract or in the list of subprocessors. The privacy statement names them. Separate several countries with commas.
